title: Salinity adjustment retained most of the temperature link to fish larva thermal composition off California in 2000-2020
abstract: We tested whether salinity accounts for the temperature link to the thermal composition of California Current fish larvae. Taxon scores came from 1978-1999 CalCOFI records. The test used 2,583 matched fish and hydrographic samples at 45 stations in 2000-2020. Models controlled station and quarter, time, sample date, local hour and sorted volume. The equal-taxon temperature slope was 0.1317 index C per water C before salinity adjustment and 0.1221 after adjustment. The adjusted 95% year-cluster interval was 0.1032 to 0.1411. Thus 92.8% of the original point slope remained. The paired reduction was 0.00954, with a year jackknife interval of 0.00187 to 0.01722. Positive adjusted slopes remained in both geographic sectors. Salinity alone did not account for most of the measured temperature link on this depth scale. This does not rule out transport without a salinity signal or establish a direct thermal cause. These slopes are not fractions of spatial tracking. Fitted local scores, capture, phenology, source water and few years limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and an external-data retrieval method are included.

display.caption: Temperature slopes before and after salinity adjustment, and residual temperature-salinity association. Intervals are individual 95% year-cluster intervals. Slopes are not fractions of spatial tracking.
